thesis: This episode argues that Costco is a unique compounder because it combines the cheapest prices with the wealthiest customer base by prioritizing member value over margin expansion. The thesis rests on the idea that Costco's 'squeaky clean' philosophy—paying employees well, respecting suppliers, and pre-selecting high-quality SKUs—creates an incredibly efficient, capital-light business model with stable growth.

claims.claim: Costco is Charlie Munger's favorite company, he sits on its board, and it combines seemingly opposite characteristics to create incredible value.
claims.quote: overview Costco is not only Charlie Munger's favorite company of all time (plus he's on the board, natch), it's an absolutely fascinating study in how seemingly opposite characteristics can combine to create incredible company value.

claims.claim: Costco has the cheapest prices of any major retailer in America while also having the wealthiest customer base.
claims.quote: For instance: Costco has the cheapest prices of any major retailer in America — and also the wealthiest customer base.

claims.claim: Costco pays hourly workers 30% above the industry norm with excellent healthcare and 401k benefits.
claims.quote: They pay their hourly workers 30% above the industry norm (and give them excellent healthcare + 401k benefits)

claims.claim: Costco is almost three times more profitable on labor than Walmart despite paying higher wages.
claims.quote: — and are almost 3x more profitable on labor than Walmart.

claims.claim: Costco stocks 40 times fewer SKUs than Walmart rivals yet sells 15 times more volume of each item.
claims.quote: Speaking of Walmart, Costco stocks 40x fewer SKUs than their Bentonville-based rivals — yet sells an average of 15x more volume of each.

claims.claim: Practically all of Costco's C-Suite executives started their careers as baggers and checkout clerks.
claims.quote: And oh yeah, practically all of Costco's C-Suite started their careers as baggers and checkout clerks!

claims.claim: Airbnb is mentioned as the reason downtown hotels are a problem, but no investment view is expressed.
claims.quote: David: I know. Airbnb is the thing. Ben: Airbnb.

claims.claim: Costco passes 89% of supplier price reductions directly to members.
claims.quote: or every dollar that Costco gets a supplier to reduce the price on something—again, tough but fair—the customer actually sees most 89% of the benefit. Costco really does just get to pass whenever they get a benefit, 89% of that benefit goes to the member.

claims.claim: Costco prioritizes providing value to members and retaining them over increasing margins.
claims.quote: The way I look at this is some companies always look for ways to make more margin. Costco specifically does the opposite. They look for ways to provide more value to members, retain them for members as longer, and get them to get their friends to be members.

claims.claim: Costco achieves lower overhead costs through efficiency rather than squeezing suppliers or underpaying.
claims.quote: They try hard across the board to get lower overhead costs through cleverness and efficiency, not through squeezing, underpaying, or anything like that.

claims.claim: Costco's philosophy is to work hard to charge customers less, a directive from Jim Sinegal to Jeff Bezos.
claims.quote: Henceforth, as of today, Amazon is a company that works hard to charge its customers less, and that is directly from Jim Sinegal.

claims.claim: Costco respects suppliers, viewing them as partners rather than targets for squeezing.
claims.quote: It is really important that they have it as one of their four main tenets, respect our suppliers.

claims.claim: Costco rewards shareholders only after obeying the law, taking care of members, employees, and suppliers.
claims.quote: Jim Sinegal articulates, if we do these four things throughout our organization, and again, those four things are obey the law, take care of our members, take care of our employees, respect our suppliers in that order, then we will achieve our ultimate goal, which is to reward our shareholders.

claims.claim: Costco maintains a squeaky clean, long-term oriented mindset with a fierce fix cap on markups.
claims.quote: The wages, the way they treat suppliers, the fierce fix cap on markups, the discipline not to raise memberships constantly. I think it's been six years between the last two times they raised the membership, even $5. It's a ludicrously squeaky clean and long-term–oriented mindset.

claims.claim: Costco views its house brand as an opportunity to provide value to members, not to capture more margin.
claims.quote: I do think, much like their 11% Target gross margin on everything, Costco looks at their house brand as an opportunity to provide value to members, not an opportunity to capture more margin for themselves.

claims.claim: Costco's low SKU count works because they pre-select high-quality items, ensuring great value without needing selection.
claims.quote: Costco makes the opposite bet. They bet that you don't need selection, as long as you ensure that everything you can buy is high quality. That is the crazy thing that has worked.

claims.claim: Costco's Kirkland Signature brand is America's largest consumer packaged brand.
claims.quote: It's America's largest consumer packaged brand.

claims.claim: Kirkland Signature sales represented a little under a quarter of Costco's top line last year.
claims.quote: Certainly, consumers agree, $52 billion of Kirkland Signature sales were done last year. That does not include the Kirkland Signature gas. Out of Costco is 230 billion top line, a little under a quarter of it was Kirkland Signature sales and closer to a third if you include the gas.

claims.claim: Costco's membership business generates an insane return on invested capital with almost no investment required.
claims.quote: To quote our friend Andrew Marks, "I basically think that Costco has decided to only be a decent return on invested capital retailer, which allows them to have an insane return on invested capital membership club business."

claims.claim: Costco has insanely stable growth on a huge capital light fee stream.
claims.quote: Again, to quote Andrew, "Insanely stable growth on a huge capital light fee stream."

claims.claim: Costco's membership model creates an amazing value for members and is also amazing for Costco's cash flow.
claims.quote: It is an amazing value for members. It is such a good value that 55% of US members now do it. But much like everything else we've talked about with Costco, it is also amazing for Costco, because they get your money at the beginning of the year further advantaging their cash flow position.

claims.claim: Executive members represent 73% of sales despite being only 45% of paid members worldwide.
claims.quote: Interestingly, 45% of paid members worldwide are executive members, but those members represent 73% of sales.

claims.claim: Costco makes money on the Costco card deal with Citi and Visa, unlike other retailers who pay fees.
claims.quote: But if you read trade publications, people seem pretty convinced that Costco is making money, which of course they are, on the deal that they caught with Citi and Visa, in order to have the Costco card be the Citi Visa card.

claims.claim: Costco generates $7.5 billion of operating income on $230 billion of sales.
claims.quote: They make $7½ billion of operating income on $230 billion of sales.

claims.claim: Costco is the third largest retailer in the US with $230 billion in revenue and 124 million members worldwide.
claims.quote: They do $230 billion in revenue. They're the third largest retailer in the US. They have 124 million members worldwide.

claims.claim: Costco has the highest revenue per square foot of any wholesaler or discount store at $1800.
claims.quote: They have the highest revenue dollars per square foot of any wholesaler or discount store. Target's about $450 per square foot of revenue. Walmart's about $600. Costco is $1800 per square foot of revenue.

claims.claim: Costco generates a huge amount of revenue dollars, though margins are lower than Apple.
claims.quote: Costco's margins are a lot lower than Apple. They're generating a huge amount of revenue dollars, not so much on the margin dollars, but as we've been talking about, that's the point.

claims.claim: Costco is described as an amazing business to own despite having low margins.
claims.quote: Ben: Yeah. Even though Costco is only an 11% gross margin business and only ever will be an 11% gross margin business, it's still a pretty amazing business to own.

claims.claim: Costco generates highly defensible operating income despite tiny margins.
claims.quote: David: Yup, especially $7½ billion of highly defensible operating income.

claims.claim: Costco is a $230 billion company that no other big company can copy.
claims.quote: co is a $230 billion company that none of the other big companies can copy. Walmart is trying and still is not succeeding at it.

claims.claim: Costco has developed significant counter positioning power as a huge incumbent.
claims.quote: David: Yup. I think where they've ended up is actually in a pretty good place and in a better place, I think, than Walmart. That place being that, no, no, the whole point is we are not an ecommerce company.

claims.claim: Costco has scale economies, process power, and a culture others have failed to replicate.
claims.quote: David: No, I think it's scale economies. Ben: Yeah. Process power, definitely. There's a culture at Costco that others have failed to replicate or haven't tried hard enough to replicate.

claims.claim: Costco has latent branding power and scale economies, choosing not to recognize short-term profits for long-term gain.
claims.quote: Ben: In a lot of ways, I think what Costco is doing is, they realize that they have latent branding power and latent scale economies. They choose not to recognize short-term profits from those. I think it's all this super long-term game, where this is why the market is willing to pay a much higher multiple for Costco than any of their competitors.

claims.claim: Costco is uniquely positioned to do well in any economic climate, including recessions and booms.
claims.quote: David: Costco, I think, is pretty uniquely positioned in that they're going to do well (I think) in any economic climate. In a recessionary environment, they're going to do well because they are the lowest priced retailer of goods out there. In a boom environment, I think they're also going to do well because of the nature of their customer base.

claims.claim: Costco has durability and a membership model that ensures revenue is not going anywhere.
claims.quote: David: Totally. Let's just say, I don't think we've talked about market cap yet. Costco does $240 billion in revenue today? Ben: Yup, and Walmart does $620 billion. David: There you go. Costco obviously trades at a much higher multiple than Walmart. You're exactly right. I think it's because of this. It's because of the durability. It's because of the membership model.
